177: The rules were very much about using your head and thinking, so even a rider weaker in jumping or performance could beat a more experienced one if they attempted harder arrows – and the results showed it. 5 riders entered on 20” bikes and the same number on 26”. Tobík Dolák won Elite 20” just ahead of his 20-inch guru Valňák, and Vlasta battled Mára Tryner for first place on the 26-inch bikes.
178: The pump track followed straight after, so the Trial riders had time to change clothes and bikes. After a few practice runs, the youngest riders on balance bikes started, and then it went all the way up to the fastest adults.
179: The finale was all about tidying up and sausages.
181: We were invited to the expo of BIGMAT, one of the big supporters of the UCI World Cups, which wanted to show its employees and partners a bit of cycling. They chose our team, for which we thank them. The bit of time pressure didn't throw us, we fitted into the space and didn't destroy any of the expensive lasers and LED screens. This time we didn't use our traditional obstacles but stylishly rode on classic pallets, and Vlasta even put on a BigMat T-shirt. He was backed up by Marek Tryner in his first exhibition after his knee injury, Tobík Dolák, who ended up as a volunteer, and Lukáš Valný, who for the first time in his life experienced a technical problem during an exhibition, when his chain snapped after maybe the first 3 jumps on a brand-new bike. Not a great advert for that X9 range.
182: Thanks for the invitation and the luxurious photos and video.
183: Weekend camps for women and men
184: This weekend was full not only of exhibitions but also of camps. On Saturday women and girls developed their skills. Sunday was devoted to men.
185: The weather was probably more pleasant for the ladies. It didn't rain, but let's be honest – it was cold. A really wide range of female bikers came together, but each found her own thing. Basic technique, balance, the pump track and berms were just the start. Gradually the women also took on smaller drops, steps and benches.
186: From the men, riding in occasional rain (fortunately it only rained for about an hour of net time), we expected a bit of respect. In the park it was a bit of a struggle, but in the forest they showed they weren't afraid to step out of their own shadow. They handled drops into gullies, a double and a few rooty descents with confidence.
187: We hope everyone moved forward a bit and found out what to work on and practise. During the camps there was already talk of buying new bikes, changing pedals and buying protectors. Thanks also to everyone for the positive feedback on the spot – we'll look forward to any further camps or individual coaching.
188: A few photos from Katarína below; the rest, including videos, we're sending directly to the participants.
189: Besides the camps, our team riders were also busy at exhibitions in Svojetice and Lomnice nad Lužnicí – an ideally filled weekend for most of our riders :)
190: Exhibition and workshop at the St Michael's Festival in Litvínov
191: The town of Litvínov invited us to its traditional St Michael's Festival, which takes place at several locations in this beautifully developing town. Our exhibition and workshop were in the centre of the sports zones in the local chateau park, right opposite the mobile stage. Unfortunately, as soon as we arrived it was clear that Vlasta, Martin and Matouš were in for a tough time. Rain, rain and a temperature you wouldn't send a dog out in. There was nothing to do but set everything up and wait until the afternoon to see if spectators would come.
192: The spectators came – and so did the rain. The guys and participants fought bravely, and even in total rain the workshop ran at full speed. We had to change the exhibition plan, and the first show took place on the stage, where Martin Šimůnek dared to jump even on the wet, slippery surface.
193: About an hour later the sun peeked out for a moment, and Vlasta and Matouš got their bikes out to jump for the local TV crew. Vlasta then did a small demonstration on the stage and the jumps over the tape, finishing a little above 125 cm, which isn't bad at all given the conditions. Matouš warmed up on the obstacles, with the only condition being that he couldn't jump down to the ground, which was one big mud bath. He warmed up nicely, even with the spectators' support, but at the moment of the real exhibition what came? ….. A total cloudburst, which was also the end of this event. We simply did our best, the organiser thanked us and so did the spectators for our courage. Thanks for the invitation – and next year without rain.
194: Opening of the Jahodnice bike park – Prague
195: We opened the Prague mini bike park in Jahodnice, where the local kiosk was also opening. The exhibition by Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček, Lukáš Valný and the little ones from the club attracted lots of spectators, who also came to ride the pump track, skills centre and jumps. After the show we joined in and tested how demanding the local jumps are – not exactly small for full-suspension bikes. Our sound system was used at the event and we signed a few autographs for local riders. Thanks for the invitation{1}{2}
196: A load of 4 exhibitions across the country
198: Our travelling marathon of exhibitions started on Wednesday at the sports games for athletes with disabilities, right away with full firepower of 4 Trial bike riders (Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček, Matouš Balík, Lukáš Pařízek and Tobík Nenadál as the youngest of the group) plus Dalibor Šulc as a moto-trial rider. The athletes with disabilities ranged from 18 to over 80 years old and were a truly great and grateful audience that appreciated every attempt the guys made. It was great to bring them a little joy and experiences, of which they had plenty at this event thanks to a great organising team.
200: One of this year's first corporate events, at the open days of Statech (forklifts and aerial work platforms), was led by Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and Martin Šimůnek. There was even jumping over a platform, which surprised the guys when they found out that, when extended, it isn't quite as stable as you'd expect :) Jumping down from it was a bit of a challenge, but Martin Šimůnek, who took it on, managed everything and survived.
202: After the north of the country we headed to more distant corners of Moravia. On Friday Matouš Balík and Vlasta set off towards Holešov, where the traditional felling of the maypole was taking place in the picturesque village of Rymice. It came down just as they arrived, so the guys saw it hit the road in front of their car. The exhibition then took place by the stage at the local municipal office. The local crowd, young and old, enjoyed the event and cheered like crazy throughout our exhibition. We also battled the slippery surface of the outdoor dance floor in front of the stage, and there were some impressive performances over the final tape from both Matouš and Vlasta.
204: Our team was already in Zubří back in 2017, and the locals chose us again to celebrate the 10th anniversary of this local event. The beautiful athletics grounds of the local school were complemented by sunny, hot weather and a huge turnout of spectators, who even had a grandstand for more comfortable viewing of the rich programme prepared by the organisers. After almost 4 hours of driving, Lukáš Valný and Vlasta took care of the event, riding a 30-minute exhibition including competitions for kids and jumping over the tape. Thanks to everyone for your support, and congratulations to the young athletes on taking part and on their placings.
205: An exhibition series to end the summer holidays
206: The second-to-last Saturday of the summer holidays brought us a small three-course series. We visited a fairly big corporate event in northern Bohemia with Martin Šimůnek, Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček and Matouš Balík. Vlasta and Matouš then headed to a real village event in Mečeříž, where the local crowd was waiting for them at the 'Farewell to the Holidays' event. Martin Šimůnek continued on a solo ride in Králův Dvůr, where he let himself be egged on into jumping off a shipping container converted into toilets :)
207: In the morning it looked like a rainy day, but in the end the weather was 100% perfect – which can't be said of the following few days.
208: When a Trial rider wins the downhill
209: Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček's report from the exhibition in Rakovník, where he, Lukáš Valný and Martin Šimůnek fell victim to a downhillers' conspiracy 🙂
210: {1}"Rakovnické cyklování is one of the big cycling events, normally allowing riders to start in 7 disciplines – from XC to the Downtown urban downhill. Unfortunately the coronavirus affected events like this too, so the organiser had to keep participant numbers down. Anyway, the event went ahead, and a day full of action awaited me, Martin Šimůnek and Lukáš Valný. {2}
211: {1}Originally we only went for 3 exhibition shows, and in the gap between the 2nd and 3rd we planned to test the local trails. It all ended differently – after we tried the footbridge over the local lake, where a crossing race was to take place the next day, the organisers of the downhill part offered us a ride in the exhibition downhill race instead of the trails. None of us had ever ridden downhill, and since the course was short and had no jumps, we said why not. The organisers even moved the start for us so we could make our last exhibition show.{2}
212: {1}Practice was great, and the tight corners probably gave us a bit of an advantage, because anyone who could get through on the front wheel gained a lot. It was practically a pure technique downhill. Based on practice I personally thought Lukáš Valný would be on the podium, but what do I know. Martin Šimůnek's 10-year-old Remedy is a bit worn out, and he was a bit out of place on 26”, but…. A race is a race and Martin has it in his blood. Without a front brake he still took 8th place out of 15 riders. Lukáš Valný was second after the first run but finished 4th in the end. At the awards ceremony we had long since changed and were practising back on our Trial bikes (it takes a moment to get used to them again), so we found it strange that they were calling us to the podium. The announcement of the downhill winner was a bit of a shock for everyone, including me. I was the only one who somehow got under 20 seconds, and with a relaxed ride I won. At first I thought they were joking (it would be just like the guys), but after checking the results I went up on the podium for the diploma. So among my dreams come true, besides Trial titles, I can now tick off a win in a DH race :D Here's to chance and Trial skills.{2}"
213: 20–21/5 – Exhibitions for Pražské služby, Strupčice and ON Semiconductor
214: We spent the weekend of 20–21 May on the bike again, but this time in nice weather that accompanied us on our long journeys. On Saturday the traditional Pražské služby event took place in Malešice, where Vlasta and Michal Budský rode together with parkour athletes and freestyle guys. The first show was by the ramp and the second right in front of the main stage. Besides the adrenaline on bikes, we got some traffic adrenaline as a bonus. Mini cars for teenage drivers were being tested at the event, driving near our obstacles, and while we were setting up, one of the cars crashed into the obstacles and pushed them together just as Vlasta was between them. Luckily the driver slammed on the brakes, so only the car's lights suffered and Vlasta went to change his underwear.
215: After the event in Malešice, Vlasta shot off without Michal to Strupčice and its luxurious swimming pool complex. Who would have thought such a small village could have such a nice sports complex. The whole event, headed by Martin Šimůnek, was a bit more intimate than the others but superbly prepared. We stretched it out a bit with competitions for the spectators and rewarded young bikers with signed cards.
216: Sunday was all about a trip to Wallachia, where one of the world's largest chip manufacturers was celebrating. Unfortunately the professionally prepared event was disrupted at the end by an approaching storm. Luckily improvisation is our domain, and right after arriving Vlasta and Michal prepared a backup option under a tent instead of the outdoor show. It looked as if it would be unnecessary, but in the end it really did rain and we rode mainly under the tent. At the end there was some egging on, and a jump from the trailer over a new Škoda Enyaq was prepared. In the wet it was a bit close to the windscreen, but in the end even a double attempt worked out 🙂
217: During the week we rode a few individual training sessions and checked the route for the camps, so there was plenty of fun.
218: TOYOTA Motors, THT.cz and Zákupy corporate events
219: {1}September events – TOYOTA Motors, THT.cz and Zákupy corporate events{2}
220: September was crazy right from the start, and the weather did its thing with our calendar. But that's nothing compared to the disaster that hit many people across the Czech Republic, and unfortunately the water didn't avoid us either (though only on a small scale). Events planned for the dates of the floods were of course all cancelled, and some others still being booked were cancelled too because of the clean-up.
221: At the start of the rains we practically only managed a corporate event for THT.cz, a manufacturer of fire and rescue vehicles. The event was indoors, so there was no problem, and we even managed to include a fire trailer, which they slightly modified for us. Vlasta's participation was in doubt because of a sprained ankle, but a bit of luck and his colleague Martin Šimůnek got him through the pain.
222: On this last weekend, when the worst has hopefully been averted / survived, we rode an exhibition for the guys from the Czech Olympic Committee and the partner of our Olympians – vehicle manufacturer TOYOTA in Kolín, right at their plant. Unfortunately the grassy area was still a bit waterlogged, so the exhibition had to be built so that the riders rode on the ground as little as possible. So we connected the stage to our obstacles and trailer. The ground was taken over by our Trial baby Marty Kabeláč, who showed adults and kids what a 7-year-old nipper can do. Martin Šimůnek and Vlasta Kabeláč Čiháček then went wild on the obstacles in two shows. In Martin's case you could say he was breaking chains – because that's exactly what he managed when jumping from obstacle to obstacle. Luckily nothing was broken, and by some miracle he managed to walk away and host the rest of the show. During the second show the area in front of the obstacles dried out a bit, so we could hold a tape-jump competition with the spectators. The Trial part was part of a mini Olympic village where competitions took place as part of a sports day. Thanks for the invitation.
